messages:
sam: heads-up: after last kernel-selector change I'm seeing a latency regression for AWQ weight-only models on dedicated nodes. p50 up ~20%, p95 spikes ~80% for seq_len=1024 workloads. filing here before i start bisecting :grimacing:

jia: ugh. rough. which model / group_size / batch shape? any KV cache signals?

sam: repro on redwood/llama2-70b-awq (group_size=64 default). workload: conv-like chat clients with many short turns -> many cache hits but occasional long context requests. KV hit rate ~88%. CPU profiler shows increased time in "pack_weights_and_alloc" and a new path in kernel_selector: `prefer_generic_unpacked` chosen for some layers.

perf-bot: automated-summary: commit 5f3b2a7 changed kernel selection heuristic to prefer shared-unpack for shapes with high batch variance. Telemetry: `pack_overhead_ms` +7ms median, `kv_cache_evictions` +0.6% in last deploy window.

matt: saw this in offline traces too. root cause looks like interaction: when AWQ weight-only uses group_size=64 the runtime chooses an unpack-based kernel to maximize reuse across lanes, but that increases temporary buffer allocations and extra memcpy for smaller groups. For short-turn traffic the amortization disappears -> net win becomes net loss.

sam: can you paste the profiler flame?

matt: here's the trimmed snippet (hot funcs):
```
0. pack_weights_and_alloc  38.2%
1. kernel_selector::choose  12.5%
2. kv_cache::read_hotpath   8.1%
3. async_prefetcher       6.9%
4. generic_unpacked_eval  5.7%
```

jia: interesting that kv_cache read is lower than pack time. suggests IO/alloc is the blocker, not KV lookup. did we change allocator behavior recently?

matt: allocator PR earlier this month switched some temp buffers to host-pinned cudaMallocManaged for cross-stream transfers. That made large-batch throughput nicer but small-batch latency worse due to page faults and driver syncs.

sam: so combined effect: kernel_selector picks unpack path + allocator causes pagefaults -> p95 blowup. makes sense.

jia: quick mitigation: - revert allocator change on the dedicated pool nodes OR - force fastpath packed kernel for weight-only AWQ models via model metadata flag. which is faster to roll out?

matt: model metadata flag is low-risk and can be shipped in 1-2 hours: add `prefer_packed_kernel: true` for models with quantization=awq and weight_only=true. ops can flip per-pool. revert allocator needs infra change + node rebuild.

sam: new test: run batch sweep with shapes: {batch:1..8, seq:64,512,1024} w/ group_size=32/64 and both allocator modes. I'll run in perf lab.

perf-bot: queued job perf/sweeps/1737000000-allocator-kvpack with priority=high. ETA results ~20m.

matt: also recommend adding a microtest that asserts kernel_selector chooses packed kernel for weight-only AWQ with small batch shapes (unit: runtime_kernel_selection_test). prevents future regresses.

jia: agree. note on calibration: AWQ calibration (per-group stats) is sensitive to group_size. switching default to 32 improved packing contiguity in earlier experiments but worsened quant error. need to balance perf vs quality. we'll keep group_size=64 for quality but force packed kernel to get perf, then explore lowering group_size with better calibration sampling later.

sam: action items: 1) matt add prefer_packed_kernel model flag + unit test 2) perf lab run and share numbers 3) ops hold allocator revert but ready if needed 4) monitor KV eviction metric (perf-bot) 5) follow-up spike to see if GPTQ models behave similarly (sam)

jia: thumbs-up. if perf lab shows >10% p50 improvement we roll to canary tonight.

perf-bot: perf/sweeps/1737000000-allocator-kvpack finished. quick summary: prefer_packed_kernel yields p50 -18%, p95 -35% for AWQ/64 on dedicated nodes, KV evictions unchanged.

sam: nice. i'll open the rollout PR and include the unit test and a short note in release notes about the allocator interaction.

matt: will also add a telemetry alert: if pack_overhead_ms > 5ms for >1% of requests trigger paging a runbook.

jia: add a comment about GPTQ: its packing tends to favor different alignment; we'll run separate sweep. closing here until PR lands. :tada:
